canonicalDependencyTrace.disposition: vaultDataEligibleSql/vaultBinaryAvailableSql/vaultDispositionChoiceSql -> eligible or matching with literal kind vault -> alias(d). The vault arm does not execute recordedLineageEligibleSql; that imported dependency serves captured/upload paths only.
canonicalDependencyTrace.version: supersededSql(d) -> VALID_LINK(succ,d); these audited aliases are source-code literals. supersededSql itself does not validate arbitrary aliases, so this finding cannot authorize nonliteral future callers.
canonicalDependencyTrace.programLock: reserveCatalogWrite -> lockDocumentDispositionProgram supplies organization/program IDs as separate values binds; no returned fragment enters any counted interpolation.
canonicalDependencyTrace.suggestionUpdate: Governance UPDATE strings SUGGEST/SUGGEST_WITH_VECTOR contain only fixed columns and $1..$13. sql(true/false) selects one of those constants. keyData JSON, vector literal, actor, attribution and document hashes are all values-array binds. This variable-query path is outside the gate regex but was manually reviewed.

limitations: The ratchet is a coarse count and does not inspect value semantics or caller provenance.

The gate cannot generally see preassembled SQL variables or string concatenation; this audit reviewed local clause builders and governance fixed UPDATE selection but is not a repository-wide injection proof.
Counts and findings apply only to the exact hashed sources and listed helper dependencies.
Fixed alias/fragment safety does not prove authorization, RLS effectiveness, regulatory compliance or provider delivery.
No app, gate, baseline, branch, index or remote state is modified by this audit.
